messages:
ops-bot: INCIDENT 🔔 - GPU OOMs causing container restarts in pool-gpu-us-west-2a. Alert rate: 18/min since 2026-03-15T02:10Z. Prefill OOM signature in agent logs. Paging oncall: maria

maria: acked. seeing container restarts across 3 nodes in the pool. stack: runtime v1.12.4.

zhang: pulling logs now. looks like long-context prefill spikes — many requests with prefill_token_count > 120k. CUDA OOM followed by container restart (OOM killer).

leo: any customer impact yet?

maria: support reports ~12 customer 5xx errors in last 8 mins. two dedicated customers on that pool had degraded throughput. overall traffic still up but those heavy requests are tailing.

sam: confirming — customer enterprise-42 reported streaming disconnects and retries. Logs show "prefill failed: cuda out of memory" then immediate 502 returned by container.

zhang: quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle/deny any incoming prefill > 80k tokens at the edge 2) enable routing fallback for heavy-context requests to cpu-fallback group or smaller model variant 3) throttle prefill concurrency on pool-gpu-us-west-2a to avoid node saturation.

maria: doing 1 & 3 now. applying egress / rate-limit rule.

leo: I'll patch routing policy to send >80k to model-micro (cpu) and add 503 with Retry-After to clients we can't route.

maria: running command to set runtime cap (temp):

```
# set a transient cap for prefill tokens on the gateway
redwoodctl config set --scope pool-gpu-us-west-2a PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP=80000 --ttl 30m
```

ops-bot: audit: config change PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP=80000 applied by maria at 2026-03-15T02:17Z

sam: support outbound to enterprise-42: "we're applying protective rate limits; you may see request rejections for very long prompts while we mitigate". They acknowledged.

zhang: rolling a hotpatch to runtime to improve early-trim during prefill. hotfix build: runtime-hotfix/1.12.5-hotprefill (sha a1b2c3d). This introduces a conservative prefill-trim that drops trailing context beyond 90k tokens during prefill stage to keep KV cache size bounded. Preparing canary on 1 node.

leo: canary deploy started on node gpu-uw2-07. observing memory and OOM counts.

maria: metrics: OOM count in pool down from 18/min to 4/min after the PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP change + routing fallback. container restarts reduced. still seeing occasional spikes when big bursts hit simultaneously.

zhang: patch logs from canary:

```
2026-03-15T02:21:12Z runtime: prefill accepted 98765 tokens -> trimmed 8740 tokens to meet cap
2026-03-15T02:21:12Z runtime: kv_cache footprint 1.4GB
2026-03-15T02:21:12Z runtime: allocation successful
```

maria: starting rolling update to apply hotfix to remaining nodes in pool (gradual, 1 node at a time). will keep PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP in place until steady for 15m.

leo: also added a temporary admission controller rule to reject requests with header X-PREFILL-TOKENS > 200k because those were single-request storms causing node flaps.

sam: customers impacted list: enterprise-42 (degraded, notified), startup-alpha (2 errors, no sustained impact). we should draft a short incident email for enterprise relays.

maria: incident timeline so far:
- 02:10Z: spikes begin, ops-bot alerts
- 02:12Z: oncall paged (maria)
- 02:14Z: initial investigation shows prefill token spikes >120k
- 02:17Z: PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP=80000 applied + routing fallback for >80k to cpu variant
- 02:19Z: OOM rate down ~70%
- 02:22Z: hotfix canary applied; positive signals
- 02:24Z: rolling update started

zhang: post-mortem/action items I propose:
- short term: add edge-level prefill token header enforcement (reject >100k) and keep PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP until runtime v1.12.5 is fully rolled out (owner: maria)
- infra: increase KV cache eviction aggressiveness for prefill stage (owner: zhang, PR target 48h)
- product: consider user-visible guidance & SDK client-side prompt trimming for very large contexts (owner: product)

leo: agree. add a metric alarm for prefill_token_count 95th > 60k sustained over 5m.

ops-bot: NOTE: escalation to SE team for impacted enterprise customers advised.

sam: drafting customer note now, will sync with maria for accurate ETA.

maria: current status: hotfix rolling, PREFILL_TOKEN_CAP in place, routing fallback active, OOMs trending down. paging oncall cleared but monitoring until 03:00Z. will update incident channel with final conclusion + postmortem link.

support-bot: incident tracker updated: incident-2026-03-15-3456789012 (severity: P2).

leo: quick FYI — we also observed one node with GPU driver transient error concurrent with OOMs; driver logs show occasional nvlink timeout. adding postmortem note to check firmware/drivers on that node family.

maria: thanks team. if anyone sees a regression ping in this thread.

zhang: PR for hotfix: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pull/412 (includes tests and canary results). planning full rollout at 02:40Z if stable metrics hold.

maria: I'll keep monitoring. marking interim mitigation as successful for now.

support-bot: incident status changed -> monitoring.

sam: sending customer update: "We've applied protective limits and a hotfix; you may see short rejections for very large prompts while we complete the roll. We'll follow up when fully resolved."

maria: final: rolling complete at 02:39Z, OOMs down to baseline, container restarts stopped. will open full postmortem ticket with timeline + root cause analysis. closing oncall.

ops-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED ✅ at 2026-03-15T02:39Z (duration 29m)
